verdict.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive, so you need your own Developer Hub app, and you can only create one from a developer sandbox account. You can connect your own sandbox, and share a private app by direct link, with no review. A public Marketplace app needs a listing and a demo video, and review can take up to 21 business days. One report puts it at about 35. The review has no security assessment.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1 hour to reach a working connection. Expect 1-2 days to prepare a Marketplace submission: legal pages, pricing page, images and a demo video.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes once your sandbox account exists
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account or a private app. Up to 21 business days for a public Marketplace app (Pipedrive's figure); about 35 business days has been reported.

gates.name: Developer sandbox + Developer Hub app
gates.unlocks: Get a client_id and client_secret, plug them into Composio, and connect your own sandbox company.
limits: You need a developer sandbox account before the Developer Hub appears in settings
Pipedrive can refuse sandbox signup at its sole discretion
The sandbox is deleted if you create no app within 45 days, or if within six months you neither publish a public app nor make a private app live
Access tokens expire after 60 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use

gates.name: Private app (direct installation link) / pre-review testing
gates.unlocks: Share a direct, unlisted installation link with other users without going through app approval. You can also install a public app yourself to test it before you submit it.
limits: Private apps are unlisted and shared only through a direct installation link
You cannot change the app type (public or private) after registration
Only a global admin can enable an app for other users in the company (third-party source)
A community thread reports Pipedrive closing sandboxes that have no published Marketplace app

gates.name: Public app approved for the Pipedrive Marketplace
gates.unlocks: Any Pipedrive customer can install the app, and you can list it on the Marketplace.
limits: Approval is at Pipedrive's discretion and its decision is final
You need a Privacy Policy page, a Terms of Service page, a pricing page, a demo video, test accounts and a reviewer contact
A local-address callback URL blocks Send to review
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days after Send to review (about 35 reported); after approval the app stays unlisted until you click Publish

steps.title: Sign up for a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
steps.detail: Sign up for a developer sandbox at developers.pipedrive.com. The Developer Hub only appears in settings for sandbox accounts. If you plan to publish, say so at signup: a community reply says sandboxes requested only for testing may not get the Marketplace Manager.
gotchas: Pipedrive can refuse sandbox signup at its sole discretion.
The sandbox is deleted if you create no app within 45 days, or if within six months you neither publish a public app nor make a private app live.
A community thread reports Pipedrive closing sandboxes with no published Marketplace app.

steps.title: Choose public vs private app type
steps.detail: Choose Public if any Pipedrive customer should be able to install the app; it then goes through Marketplace review. Choose Private for internal use; a private app skips approval and is shared by a direct installation link. Choose carefully, because you cannot change the type later.
gotchas: Every app must support OAuth 2.0. API-token integration is only for private apps.

steps.title: Create the app in Developer Hub and set the callback URL
steps.detail: In your sandbox, open Developer Hub and create an app. Under Basic info, enter the app name and a callback URL: paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. The redirect_uri sent in the authorize request must match this value exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Each app gets only one callback URL, so use a separate app for each environment.
Your app name must not suggest that Pipedrive built it.

steps.title: Select only the scopes your agent needs
steps.detail: In the app's scopes settings, choose read-only or full-access scopes for each data type the agent actually uses. Composio's defaults are contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full and projects:full; drop any you don't need. The base scope is always on. Users must accept or deny all requested scopes together.
gotchas: The admin scope fails when a non-admin installs the app, so only add it if you handle that case.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the generated client_id and client_secret from Developer Hub. In Composio, create a Pipedrive auth config with your own OAuth2 credentials, because Composio has no managed app for Pipedrive. Enter the same scopes you selected in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Run a test authorization against your sandbox
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, approve it in your sandbox company, and confirm an API call works. API calls go to the company-specific domain with the bearer token. The authorization code expires in 5 minutes. The token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth with the client_id and client_secret. Access tokens last 60 minutes and must be refreshed.
gotchas: An unknown client_id returns a 401 JSON error that points to developers.pipedrive.com. If you see it, check the credentials you pasted into Composio.

steps.title: Share with test or internal users
steps.detail: For a private app, share the direct installation link; no approval is needed. For a public app, install and test it in your sandbox before you submit it. Only a global admin can enable an app for other users in a company (third-party source).
gotchas: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use. After that, the user must reinstall the app.

steps.title: Prepare legal pages, pricing page and listing assets
steps.detail: Draft a Privacy Policy page and a Terms of Service page, and create a separate pricing page that the listing will link to. Prepare an app icon of at least 256x256 px that looks right on dark backgrounds. Prepare up to five listing images in a 16:10 aspect ratio.
gotchas: The icon must not resemble Pipedrive's icon or another Marketplace app's.

steps.title: Make the callback production-ready
steps.detail: Make sure the registered callback URL is publicly reachable and not a local address. Handle the DELETE request that Pipedrive reportedly sends to the callback URL on uninstall (third-party source). Store tokens in columns of at least varchar(768), and respect API rate limits.

steps.title: Record a demo video and prepare reviewer access
steps.detail: Record a demo video that explains how the app uses each permission and scope. Set up working test accounts and name a reviewer contact.

steps.title: Fill the listing form and click Send to review
steps.detail: Complete the Marketplace listing form, install and test the app, preview the listing, then click Send to review. You must agree to the Developer Partner Agreement.

steps.title: Wait for Pipedrive's review
steps.detail: Pipedrive says public app reviews may take up to 21 business days. A third-party blog cites a 2026 forum complaint of about 35 business days with no reviewer feedback. Approval is discretionary and the decision is final.

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: After approval the app stays unlisted until you click Publish in Developer Hub. Marketplace ranking depends on star rating and install count.

requirements.detail: You need a sandbox account to see the Developer Hub. It is deleted after periods of inactivity, and Pipedrive can terminate it at any time.

requirements.item: App name and one callback URL
requirements.detail: Basic info needs an app name and exactly one callback URL. You can save a placeholder URL first and replace it later.
Access tokens expire after 60 minutes. Refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use; each use extends them. Store tokens in columns of at least varchar(768).

requirements.item: Privacy Policy and Terms of Service pages; acceptance of the Developer Partner Agreement
Separate pricing page linked from the listing
requirements.detail: The listing must link to a separate pricing page.
Icon at least 256x256 px that looks right on dark backgrounds; up to five images at 16:10. The icon must not resemble Pipedrive's or another Marketplace app's.

requirements.item: Demo video, test accounts, reviewer contact
requirements.detail: The demo video must explain how the app uses its permissions and scopes.
A community report says Send to review is blocked when the callback URL is a local address.

scopes.effect: Always on for every app; you don't need to select it.

scopes.scope: contacts:full / leads:full / mail:full / activities:full / products:full / projects:full
scopes.effect: These are Composio's defaults. Each data type also has a read-only variant. Users must accept or deny all scopes together, so ask for the narrowest set you need, and explain each scope in the review demo video.
Requires the installing user to be a company admin. Marketplace installs are not limited to admins, so the app must handle a non-admin installer.

blockers.symptom: Developer Hub does not appear in Pipedrive settings
blockers.cause: You are not signed in to a developer sandbox account
blockers.fix: Sign up for a sandbox at developers.pipedrive.com and open the Developer Hub from that account.

blockers.symptom: No Marketplace Manager / cannot submit the app to the Marketplace
blockers.cause: According to a community reply, the sandbox was requested for testing only
blockers.fix: Contact Pipedrive through the developer community and ask them to enable Marketplace access for your sandbox.

blockers.cause: Inactivity rules: no app within 45 days, or no published public app and no live private app within six months. A community thread also reports closures of sandboxes with no published app, and Pipedrive can terminate sandboxes without notice.
blockers.fix: Create an app soon after signup, and publish or make it live within the allowed time.

blockers.symptom: Developer Hub will not let you click Send to review
blockers.cause: The callback URL is a local address
blockers.fix: Register a public callback URL, such as Composio's callback URL.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect mismatch
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the request differs from the single callback URL registered in Developer Hub
blockers.fix: Set the Developer Hub callback URL to exactly the callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Users must reconnect after a long period of inactivity
blockers.cause: The refresh token expired after 60 days without use
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens regularly. If one has already expired, the user must reinstall the app.

blockers.symptom: Wrong app type chosen (public vs private)
blockers.cause: You cannot change the app type after registration
blockers.fix: Register a new app with the correct type and replace the credentials in Composio.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive, so you must register your own app in Developer Hub from a sandbox account, even for testing. Give its client_id and client_secret to a Composio OAuth2 auth config. Register Composio's callback URL as the app's single callback URL, and choose scopes deliberately rather than relying on Composio's defaults. Use a private app for internal use without review; use a public app, which needs Marketplace review, if any Pipedrive customer should be able to connect.

open_questions: Can users in other Pipedrive companies install a private app through its direct link, or is it limited to your own company? The docs describe private apps as internal-only.
Is a paid Pipedrive plan needed for the sandbox? A community source says so; the official docs do not say.
No install cap for apps that have not been reviewed was found, and the rate-limit page was not fetched.
Is PKCE supported? The fetched docs only show Basic auth with client_secret and an optional state value.
Pipedrive's docs do not confirm that Composio's default redirect (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) is the URL to register. Use the callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.
Composio's default scopes have not been checked against Pipedrive's scope catalog or your agent's actual needs.
The official pages fetched mention no security assessment, domain verification or minimum install count. The reported review times beyond 21 days come only from a third-party blog.
